newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle 1996 sales rise, sees 1997 profit gain.
newsitem.headline: Nestle 1996 sales rise, sees 1997 profit gain.

text.p: Nestle SA's sales grew 7.1 percent to a record 60.5 billion Swiss francs ($43 billion) in 1996 as volume gains teamed up with the weakening Swiss franc to boost global revenues, the world's biggest food company said Tuesday.

It gave an upbeat assessment for 1997 as well, forecasting sales volume would keep growing. "Barring adverse currency developments, the group should therefore register another increase in sales and profit," it said in a statement.
The company, based in Vevey, Switzerland, gave no profit figures for 1996, but said net profit growth should outstrip the rate at which sales increased.
"For the first time since 1993, exchange rates had a moderately positive effect of 1.4 percent," Nestle said. "Sales volume growth, excluding acquisitions and disinvestments, was 2.7 percent."
It said the Asia/Pacific region, Africa and the Middle East all registered strong volume growth. Growth was above average in Europe, due primarily to rapid expansion in central and eastern Europe.

"In the Americas, Latin America achieved above-average growth, whereas the U.S. market's overall growth did not live up to expectations, particularly due to transitional problems in the beverage division," it said.
